title: Adaptive Loop Tiling for Heterogeneous Architectures
problem: Computational kernels on heterogeneous CPU-GPU systems require different optimization strategies, and static tile sizes are suboptimal across varying hardware configurations. Manual tuning of tile parameters for diverse architectures is impractical at scale.
motivation: Heterogeneous architectures are ubiquitous in HPC systems. Finding optimal tile sizes for different hardware combinations directly impacts performance, but current static approaches cannot adapt to system-specific characteristics.
method: The technique uses runtime profiling to monitor kernel performance and automatically adjust tile sizes during execution. It adapts tiling parameters based on observed performance and hardware properties of the CPU-GPU system.
key_novelty: Adaptive tile sizing framework that dynamically optimizes loop tiling parameters for heterogeneous systems using runtime profiling, eliminating manual per-architecture tuning.
contributions: Adaptive loop tiling framework for heterogeneous CPU-GPU systems
Runtime profiling methodology to determine optimal tile sizes dynamically
Automatic kernel optimization reducing manual parameter tuning effort
primary_theme: Runtime-adaptive tiling for heterogeneous CPU-GPU systems
